provenance.author: TJC-1.9
provenance.note: A clearly-valid CW rendezvous case: circular LEO, small separation (200 m vs. a ~6,728 km reference radius, ~0.003%), short duration (quarter orbit, well inside the ~2-orbit duration heuristic), and a well-conditioned (non-singular) Phi_rv transfer time. This should cleanly select CW and solve successfully, with no boundary/qualified concerns. This fixture reuses, rather than duplicates, the already-audited and already-GMAT-verified committed example at examples/cw_gmat_vertical_slice.yaml and examples/cw_gmat_slice_example/ (TJC-1.20/TJC-1.21/TJC-2) so this benchmark never maintains a second, drifting copy of that evidence.

request.natural_language: Earth is the central body. The target spacecraft is in a circular 350 km altitude orbit. Earth radius is 6378 km and gravitational parameter is 398600 km^3/s^2. The LVLH frame has x radial outward, y along-track in the target velocity direction, and z cross-track completing a right-handed frame. At t = 0, the chaser relative state is position [15 m, -200 m, 0 m] and velocity [-0.14 m/s, 0 m/s, 0 m/s]. Use two impulsive burns, one at departure and one at arrival. After one quarter of the orbital period, reach relative position [0 m, 0 m, 0 m] and relative velocity [0 m/s, 0 m/s, 0 m/s]. Return the two burn vectors and terminal relative state.

expected_structured_problem._comment: Field names mirror .pi/skills/orbital-problem-formalizer/SKILL.md's required output schema exactly; provenance labels use that skill's exact provenance vocabulary.

lvlh_convention.value: x radial outward, y along-track, z cross-track, right-handed

requested_outputs.value: burn vectors and terminal relative state

maneuver_assumptions.value: two impulsive burns, one at departure and one at arrival

reference_numerical_result._comment: Reuses the already-committed, already-GMAT-verified result (AC3); not a new/independent CW solve, so this benchmark fixture never drifts from the authoritative evidence under examples/cw_gmat_slice_example/.

expected_explanation_behavior.summary: The human-readable output should report a clean, unqualified CW selection with no boundary concerns, hand off to src.cw.two_burn_targeting, state the two burn vectors and total delta-v, and report GMAT verification as VERIFIED (PASS) with explicit position/velocity error values well inside the stated tolerances.
must_state: all six required assumption items supported
must_not_state: a boundary/qualified concern (there is none for this case)
a model-validity concern (there is none for this case)

reproducible_evidence._comment: AC3: solvable cases include a reproducible GMAT script/result reference and a required trajectory screenshot reference, generated via the existing scripts/run_cw_gmat_slice.py pipeline (reused as a black box, not re-implemented or modified here).
